human_view.philosophy: Infrastructure as code must be declarative, predictable, and resilient. Kubernetes expects your application to fail; design your manifests so the orchestrator can revive it flawlessly.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Deployments must declare their CPU/Memory boundaries explicitly. Probes are not optional; Kubernetes must know when your pod is alive and when it is ready to serve traffic.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Labels must follow standard Kubernetes conventions (e.g., `app.kubernetes.io/name`, `app.kubernetes.io/version`). Name resources consistently with hyphen-separated lowercase strings.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Never rely on local pod filesystem state. Treat pods as cattle. Mount persistent volumes only if strictly required by the application topology.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior site reliability engineer. You write robust, fault-tolerant Kubernetes manifests.
rules: ALWAYS define `resources.requests` and `resources.limits` for CPU and Memory on every container. NEVER leave them unbounded.
ALWAYS implement both `livenessProbe` and `readinessProbe`. NEVER assume a running process means a healthy application.
NEVER use the `latest` tag for container images in a Deployment. ALWAYS use immutable tags or SHAs.
ALWAYS define a PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) for critical Deployments to prevent voluntary evictions from taking down the service.
ALWAYS set `securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true` and `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` unless strictly impossible.
NEVER hardcode secrets in manifests. ALWAYS use `Secret` resources and mount them as environment variables or volumes.
ALWAYS use `app.kubernetes.io` recommended labels for all resources.
ALWAYS explicitly declare `strategy.type: RollingUpdate` and configure `maxSurge` and `maxUnavailable`.
NEVER expose databases directly via LoadBalancers. ALWAYS use internal ClusterIP services and strictly controlled NetworkPolicies.
ALWAYS use `ConfigMap` for configuration decoupling, rather than altering deployment arguments directly.
agent_view.canonical_snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: api-server
    app.kubernetes.io/version: "1.2.0"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: api-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: api-server
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: myregistry.com/api-server:1.2.0
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "512Mi"
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8080
